tldr: Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro surfaced after Arena testing on Oct 23 and launched Oct 24 as a multi-trillion-parameter flagship served via API. A botched launch forced a quota reset and apology, and third-party hosts started listing it within days.
whats_new: Huawei Ascend now supports LoRA fine-tuning of Kimi K3.1 Pro on a 128-card Atlas 950 SuperPoD, following Moore Threads day-zero serving support and the Nov 5 open-weights release.
why_it_matters: Open weights plus day-0 vLLM and non-NVIDIA accelerator support make Kimi K3.1 Pro a self-hostable and fine-tunable frontier-class option, though at roughly 1.56TB of weights it is a large-cluster deployment.

status.detail: Weights are public with conditional commercial use, and inference and fine-tuning support is spreading across engines, clouds and domestic Chinese accelerators.

beats.headline: Kimi K3.1 appears after Arena testing and is compared to Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra
Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro as its new flagship
beats.summary: Coverage describes a roughly 3T-parameter model and a faster Highspeed API tier.

beats.headline: User quota complaints force a reset and an apology
beats.summary: Moonshot reset Kimi K3.1 Pro quotas, then publicly apologised for the botched launch and restored user quotas.

beats.headline: Third-party platforms add Kimi K3.1 Pro
beats.summary: NEAR AI Cloud, ZenMux and Verda Inference list it, and vLLM ships day-0 support.

beats.headline: Moonshot releases full Kimi K3.1 Pro weights
beats.summary: Reports cite free 1.56TB weights on Hugging Face with commercial use permitted under conditions.

beats.headline: Training and domestic-hardware ecosystem forms around the weights
beats.summary: vLLM covers zero-mismatch async RL with Kimi K3.1, Moore Threads adds day-zero serving, and Huawei Ascend adapts it for LoRA fine-tuning.

open_questions: What are the exact commercial-use conditions in the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights license?
Do independent benchmarks confirm the claimed closeness to closed frontier models?
Will Moonshot's hosted API quotas and the Highspeed tier stay stable after the launch reset?
Which serving stacks beyond vLLM and Ascend publish production-ready Kimi K3.1 Pro recipes?
take_for_builders: Read the weights license commercial-use conditions before planning self-hosting, budget for a large multi-GPU cluster given the 1.56TB checkpoint, and keep a fallback model since the hosted API had quota problems at launch.
